Chapter 9. The Arena—Living Brave Every Day.
When you hear the word "arena," what comes to mind? For a lot of us, it’s a place of action—a stage where things get real. In the heart of rising strong, this metaphor comes alive. Life, with all its messiness and unpredictability, is our arena. Every day hands us new challenges, new chances to show up, to be seen, and to take the risk of being vulnerable.
Picture a young entrepreneur, launching her very first business. She’s riding this wild wave of excitement and fear. Each pitch she gives, every setback she faces, and all those moments she questions herself—they’re all tests of her courage. And what she discovers is powerful: bravery doesn’t mean you’re not scared. It means you keep moving forward, even when you are.
Now, here's something most folks don’t realize. So often, we choose comfort over courage without even thinking about it. The arena isn’t a place where things are certain or safe. It’s where we risk, where we’re exposed, and yes, where we might fail. But it’s also the only place where we truly grow, where we make real connections, and where we find meaning.
Think about a parent, speaking up for his child at school. He feels that vulnerability—the fear of being judged, the worry he might make things worse. But he steps into the arena anyway. He has that tough conversation and stands up for what matters. Sure, he doesn’t know how it’ll turn out, but just showing up? That’s a win in itself.
Living brave every day isn’t about huge, dramatic gestures. It’s about those small, everyday choices. Choosing to be honest. Asking for help when you need it. Owning up to mistakes. Saying thank you. These moments, stacked one on top of the other, create a life built on courage and resilience.
Here’s another example—a teacher, after a really tough year, decides to open up to her colleagues about her struggles. Instead of judgment, she’s met with understanding. Together, they come up with ways to support each other and their students. That simple act of vulnerability ends up changing not just her outlook, but the whole school community.
The arena is where life actually happens. It’s where we get tested, where we stumble, where we fall, and—most importantly—where we rise again. Every time you choose to show up, let yourself be seen, and risk a little vulnerability, you’re building that muscle of resilience. And that’s what living brave, every single day, is all about.
